html:
The New Zealand mountaineer who, with Tenzing Norgay, made the first confirmed climb to the top of Mount Everest on 29 May 1953.

Hillary was a beekeeper from Auckland who learned to climb in the Southern Alps. He served in the air force in the Second World War. The 1953 expedition was British, led by John Hunt, and Hillary and Tenzing were its second summit pair. The news reached London on the morning of the coronation of Elizabeth II.

He kept exploring. In 1958 his team drove farm tractors to the South Pole as part of a Commonwealth crossing of Antarctica, the first to reach it overland since Scott in 1912.

His most lasting work was in Nepal. From 1961 his Himalayan Trust built schools, clinics and bridges for the Sherpa communities of the Everest region. Hillary was modest about the climb and always called Tenzing his equal. He appears on the New Zealand five dollar note, a rare honour for a living person when it was issued.
sum: The New Zealand mountaineer who, with Tenzing Norgay, made the first confirmed climb to the top of Mount Everest on 29 May 1953.
